The maximum score will be achieved when the product of the numbers in each 2x2 subgrid is maximized. Since each cell can be either 0 or 1, the maximum product for any 2x2 subgrid is 1 (when all four cells are 1). Therefore, the maximum score is the number of 2x2 subgrids in the 10x10 grid, which is \(9 \times 9 = 81\). This is because there are 9 possible starting positions for the top-left corner of a 2x2 subgrid in both the rows and columns of the 10x10 grid. Thus, the maximum possible score of the grid is 81.
